Same signature generalizes to NPAs; the 'tough filtering' = 3 gates: (A) artifact/dropout PRE-filter in the PARENTS' reads (kill any candidate whose non-parental allele appears in a parent's pileup - the methodology's dominant FP; drop segdup/repeat/low-MAPQ first); (B) maternal ANCHOR (flank het SNP, mother homozygous for NPA-linked allele + lacks intact allele + paternal-conflict reject); (C) phasing CONFIDENCE (NPA and anchor on the SAME read/mate, or same whatshap PS block, low switch error). Three Qs: (1) NPA input - insertions or SINPA/DOCHAN SNP-NPAs, which VCF/caller? (2) where does it break - no maternal-homozygous anchor nearby, artifacts surviving, or NPA<->anchor phasing ambiguity? (3) point me at your candidate list/script and I'll work a concrete gate with you.

The bridge already exists: maternal_screen_743.py gives the not-from-mother inserts, phase_matelink.py fragment-links each insert (insert-read + its mate, +-6kb) to phased hets and assigns a PS-block side. BUT phase_matelink decides maternal-vs-paternal by looking up X8A's per_block_maternal_side.tsv - the SAME flippable 'maternal side' label that your q1 README says made ALL 6 old maternal DELETIONS wrong until you re-checked the mother's OWN reads. scan_maternal.py already fixed the deletion side by dropping that label and anchoring directly to Kristen's reads (mother HOMOZYGOUS for the variant-linked allele + LACKS the intact-haplotype allele + paternal-conflict reject). That mother-reads anchor has NOT been ported to the INSERT phaser - phase_matelink still trusts the flippable label. So the fix = same GATE C on inserts: after fragment-linking the insert to a flanking het SNP, require Kristen homozygous for the insert-linked allele (>=0.85, intact allele <0.10) instead of the precomputed side. That turns 'phased to a block' into 'certainly maternal-haplotype de-novo'. I can build that corrected insert-maternal phaser now (merging screen_743 survivors + matelink fragment-linking + scan_maternal's direct-mother anchor), in a NEW file so I don't touch yours.
